questiontext.text: What pointers does each node of a doubly linked list hold?

answer.text: Both a prev and a next pointer

feedback.text: Correct — that pair enables bidirectional traversal.
That describes a singly linked list.
A doubly linked node needs next as well as prev.

answer.text: A single pointer to the head

feedback.text: Nodes link to their neighbors, not all to the head.

generalfeedback.text: Each node stores both a prev and a next pointer, allowing traversal in both directions.

questiontext.text: Why can a doubly linked list delete a given node in O(1)?

answer.text: Its prev pointer lets you relink the predecessor without a traversal

feedback.text: Correct — you reach the predecessor directly via prev.

answer.text: Because nodes are stored contiguously in memory

feedback.text: Linked list nodes are not contiguous; that is arrays.

answer.text: Because it keeps a sorted index of all nodes

feedback.text: No index is maintained; the prev pointer is what matters.

answer.text: Because deletion always happens at the head

feedback.text: Deletion can be at any known node, thanks to prev.

generalfeedback.text: Because the prev pointer gives O(1) access to the predecessor, you can splice out a known node without searching.

questiontext.text: In a circular doubly linked list, what does the head node's prev pointer reference?

feedback.text: Correct — the ring closes with head.prev pointing to the tail.
That is only true for a one-node list, not in general.
In a circular list no pointer is null.
That is head.next, not head.prev.

generalfeedback.text: In a circular doubly linked list, head.prev points to the tail and tail.next points to the head.

questiontext.text: Compared with a singly linked list, a doubly linked list mainly adds:

answer.text: A prev pointer in each node for backward links

feedback.text: Correct — the extra prev pointer enables backward traversal.
Linked lists are not contiguous regardless of direction.
Neither list type is sorted by construction.
Linked lists still need traversal to reach an index.

generalfeedback.text: The defining addition is a per-node prev pointer, giving backward links and O(1) known-node deletion.

questiontext.text: A doubly linked list allows traversal in both directions.

feedback.text: Correct — prev and next pointers permit forward and backward traversal.
The prev pointer makes backward traversal possible.

questiontext.text: In a circular doubly linked list, the last node's next pointer is always null.

feedback.text: In the circular variant the last node's next points back to the head, not null.
Correct — the last node's next points back to the head (and head's prev to the tail).

questiontext.text: The pointer that references the preceding node is called the ______ pointer.

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.
Correct.

questiontext.text: Which statements about doubly / circular linked lists are true? (select all that apply)

answer.text: Each node stores both a prev and a next pointer

feedback.text: Yes — that is what makes it doubly linked.

answer.text: In the circular variant the last node's next points back to the head

feedback.text: Yes — and the head's prev points to the tail.

answer.text: Traversal is only possible from head to tail

feedback.text: No — the prev pointer allows backward traversal too.

answer.text: Deleting a known node requires O(n) to find its predecessor

feedback.text: No — the prev pointer gives the predecessor in O(1).

generalfeedback.text: Doubly linked: prev + next per node, bidirectional traversal, O(1) known-node deletion; circular variant wraps last-next to head.
